chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is none who owns wealth subject to zakat — palm trees, or farmland, or a vineyard — who withholds the zakat of his wealth, except that Allah will collar him with the soil of his land, to be encircled by it from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.زَكَاة: Zakat — obligatory alms-tax; here specifically applied to agricultural produce (dates, grain, grapes)
key_terms.سَبْع أَرَضِين: Seven earths — the seven layers of the earth in Islamic cosmology, indicating the depth and weight of the punishment
key_terms.قَلَّدَهُ: Collaring — the image of a yoke or collar being placed around the neck, signifying humiliation and burden
key_terms.يُطَوَّق: To be encircled/collared — passive voice indicating divine punishment, a metaphor for being weighed down by one's own withheld charity

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for withholding zakat on agricultural wealth in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a hadith from the Prophet (SAWW) warning of the severe eschatological punishment for those who withhold obligatory zakat on agricultural produce. The punishment is vividly portrayed as a physical collaring with the very soil of one's land, extending through all seven layers of the earth, which the wrongdoer must bear until the Day of Judgment. This hadith was directed at those who possessed agricultural wealth — palm groves, farms, vineyards — the primary forms of taxable wealth in 7th-century Arabia.
